feature: Responsive semi-complex model import and native Blender .blend file import

seams.what: the browser-side model validator and native picker filter
seams.evidence: the model set and picker accept list both omit blend while export uses a separate FORMATS set
seams.asks: should .blend appear only for Import Model, with export formats unchanged?

seams.what: the shared engine format contract currently used for both import and export
seams.evidence: its docstring deliberately excludes blend because opening a Blender file would replace process scene state
seams.asks: should native blend be an import-only format that appends data instead of opening/replacing the process scene?

seams.what: the operation-log boundary that accepts or rejects uploaded model suffixes
seams.evidence: every browser and MCP import reaches this local-file validation before Blender
seams.asks: should .blend use the same axis, scale and flatten options as interchange imports?

seams.evidence: all current formats call bpy operators; blend needs bpy.data.libraries loading instead of an import operator
seams.asks: which datablocks from a blend file should appear: mesh objects only, or cameras/lights/empties too?

seams.what: the atomic Blender model import transaction and post-import transform handling
seams.evidence: created objects are tracked and rolled back on failure, then mesh transforms may be flattened
seams.asks: should linked libraries remain linked, or should Forge3D append editable local copies?

seams.what: the paused owner-thread file job that turns an uploaded model into a scene operation
seams.evidence: the job already serializes Blender work but reports only coarse start and completion progress
seams.asks: what progress and completion feedback should a user see while a larger blend is loading and previewing?

seams.what: full engine snapshots flattened into browser geometry buffers
seams.evidence: every vertex, triangle, normal and UV is serialized even though the browser is a live preview rather than the authoritative model
seams.asks: may the live viewer use a deterministic lower-detail proxy while Blender, saving and export keep the complete mesh?

seams.what: the topology-change and full-scene messages sent after imports
seams.evidence: an imported model is serialized synchronously as one mesh-upsert/full-scene payload
seams.asks: should preview simplification be disclosed in the scene message and UI rather than silently dropping display triangles?

seams.what: synchronous conversion of JSON arrays into typed viewer buffers
seams.evidence: large payloads allocate full duplicate typed arrays on the browser main thread before the scene can draw
seams.asks: should ingestion remain exact for already-budgeted proxies, or add progressive chunking too?

seams.evidence: it rasterizes the entire scene every animation frame even when neither camera nor scene changed
seams.asks: should rendering become event-driven and redraw only after scene, camera, selection or texture changes?

seams.what: the CPU triangle and pixel raster loop that blocks pointer events
seams.evidence: every triangle is transformed, shaded, material-searched and rasterized on the browser main thread for every frame
seams.asks: during orbit/zoom, should the viewer temporarily reduce detail and render full preview quality after interaction ends?

seams.what: real-Blender proof for advertised model formats
seams.evidence: the current parametrization assumes every supported extension is exportable, which cannot be true for import-only blend
seams.asks: should the contract split import formats from export formats and add a real blend append test?

seams.what: the real-Chrome suite that already owns import UI flows
seams.evidence: it verifies file actions but has no semi-complex mesh responsiveness budget
seams.asks: what interaction delay should count as responsive for a semi-complex preview?
